instantiated_cells.justification: Principals must file expense statements on or before July 31 and January 31 (semiannually), not annually.
The statute specifies filing on July 31 and January 31, not monthly reporting.
The law provides a semiannual schedule (July 31 and January 31) and does not authorize another periodic frequency option for the principal expense statement.
The required principal expense statement is due twice per year, not quarterly.
Registered principals must file an expense statement on or before July 31 and January 31 covering the preceding 6-month reporting period, which is semiannual reporting.
Reporting periods are defined as fixed 6-month periods and filings are due July 31 and January 31, not three times per year tied to the legislative calendar.
Because the statute specifies only semiannual due dates (July 31 and January 31), there is no other reporting frequency to describe.
The principal registration statement must include descriptions of business activity or the principal’s nature and purposes, requiring disclosure of the nature of the business/organization.
The expense statement’s aggregate total must include compensation to lobbyists for lobbying (cash or in-kind) and reimbursements.
The expense statement requires time records and names of officials reimbursed, but it does not require reporting specific contacts/communications with officials.
Principals must report each legislative proposal, budget bill subject, proposed administrative rule number, or otherwise each topic of lobbying communications with reasonable specificity.

The expense statement must include reimbursements to covered officials (including travel) and total expenditures for personal travel and living expenses, which are categories of non-compensation costs such as transportation/lodging.
The statement includes non-compensation lobbying expenditures such as research/analysis, paid advertising to urge the public, office overhead for in-house lobbyists, and travel/living expenses.
If payments to any lobbyist exceed $200 in a reporting period, the principal must list the lobbyist’s name and address.

The expense statement requires listing each lobbyist whose total compensation/reimbursement from the principal exceeds $200 during the reporting period, identifying lobbyists representing the principal.
Neither the registration requirements nor the expense statement provisions require principals to disclose major financial contributors.
The principal registration statement must specify the principal’s name and business address.
The law requires the principal to report each legislative proposal and proposed administrative rule number in connection with which it made or intends to make a lobbying communication.
Principals must report the aggregate total amount of lobbying expenditures made and obligations incurred for lobbying by the principal and all lobbyists for the principal.
The spending report includes compensation to lobbyists and, when payments to a lobbyist exceed $200, requires reporting the total amount paid to that lobbyist.

The report requires daily itemization of time and itemized identification of certain recipients (reimbursements) and lobbyists paid over $200, demonstrating itemized rather than purely lump-sum disclosure.
Associations must report the chief executive officer and approximate number of members, but the statute does not require listing names of all sponsors or members.
When lobbying expenditures to any lobbyist exceed $200 in the reporting period, the principal must list that lobbyist’s name and address, effectively listing lobbyists employed/engaged.
